data.name: Lunar Module Eagle
data.current_location: Tranquility Base, Mare Tranquillitatis, Moon (0.67408° N, 23.47297° E)
data.description: The descent stage of Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle that carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to the surface.
data.discoveries: Enabled first human footsteps on another world.
data.legacy: A permanent monument marking the inaugural landing of humanity on another world.

data.name: Philae Lander
data.operational_period: 12–15 November 2014 (Primary 64-Hour Science Sequence; brief contact in June 2015)
data.current_location: Abydos crevice, beneath rocky overhang, Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko
data.description: Philae was the robotic lander deployed by Rosetta on 12 November 2014. After descending for 7 hours, its anchoring harpoons and thruster failed to fire, causing it to bounce twice off the comet nucleus before coming to rest in the shadowed crevice of Abydos. It completed 80% of its planned primary science sequence on battery power before entering hibernation.
data.legacy: First spacecraft to touch down on a cometary nucleus; delivered ground-truth measurements of primordial solar system chemistry.

data.name: Voyager 1 Spacecraft
data.current_location: Interstellar Space (Outer Heliosheath, ~163 AU / 24.4 billion km from the Sun)
data.description: Launched in September 1977, Voyager 1 completed historic flybys of Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980) before heading outward along a hyperbolic trajectory out of the ecliptic plane. In August 2012, Voyager 1 crossed the Heliopause to become the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. It is the most distant operational machine in human history.
data.legacy: Humanity’s premier interstellar emissary; carries the Golden Record with greetings in 55 languages and sounds of Earth; redefined our place in the cosmos.

data.name: Surveyor 3 Lander
data.current_location: Surveyor Crater, Oceanus Procellarum, Moon (3.0163° S, 23.4180° W)
data.description: Landed in a crater; later visited by Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean.
data.discoveries: Scooped trenches up to 17.5 cm deep proving soil consistency and bearing strength.
data.legacy: The camera brought back to Earth by Apollo 12 provided valuable data on long-term lunar exposure.

data.name: Spirit Rover
data.current_location: Troy sand trap, west side of Home Plate plateau, Gusev Crater, Mars (14.57° S, 175.48° E)
data.description: Spirit was the first of the twin Mars Exploration Rovers to arrive at the Red Planet, touching down inside the volcanic basin of Gusev Crater in January 2004. Defying its planned 90-sol design lifetime, Spirit explored for over 6 Earth years, climbing the Columbia Hills and uncovering ancient hydrothermal hot spring deposits.
data.legacy: Demonstrated extreme resilience in planetary exploration; proved ancient Mars had active volcanic hydrothermal systems capable of preserving biological signatures; operated for 2,210 sols (over 20 times its planned warranty).

data.name: Opportunity Rover
data.current_location: Perseverance Valley, Endeavour Crater rim, Mars (2.33° S, 354.67° E)
data.description: Opportunity touched down on Mars in January 2004 for a planned 90-day mission. Defying all expectations, the solar-powered rover operated for nearly 15 Earth years (5,111 Martian sols), traversing 45.16 kilometers across Meridiani Planum and uncovering undeniable evidence that liquid water once flowed across Mars.
data.legacy: Holds the all-time off-world distance driving record (45.16 km); proved the long-term viability of robotic field geology on other planets; transformed humanity's understanding of Martian paleoclimates.

data.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle
data.operational_period: 31 July – 02 August 1971 (3 Extravehicular Activities / 18 hr 30 min drive time)
data.description: The Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-001) was the first wheeled vehicle driven by humans on another celestial body. Built by Boeing and Delco Electronics, it allowed astronauts David Scott and James Irwin to venture 5 kilometers away from the Lunar Module Falcon, covering 27.76 kilometers across the Hadley-Apennine valley.
data.legacy: Revolutionized lunar field geology by expanding surface exploration distance by a factor of ten; paved the way for all subsequent off-world rovers.

data.name: Voyager 2 Spacecraft
data.current_location: Interstellar Space (~136 AU / 20.3 billion km from the Sun)
data.description: The only human spacecraft to explore Uranus and Neptune.
data.discoveries: Discovered 16 new moons and multiple ring systems across outer planets.
data.legacy: Entered interstellar space in November 2018, continuing to transmit cosmic ray data.

data.name: Sojourner Rover
data.current_location: Carl Sagan Memorial Station, Ares Vallis, Mars (19.33° N, 33.55° W)
data.description: First wheeled rover on another planet, measuring only 65 cm long and weighing 10.5 kg.
data.discoveries: Confirmed basaltic volcanic rocks resembling andesite on Mars.
data.legacy: Established the foundational mobility archetype for Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity.

data.name: Ingenuity Helicopter
data.current_location: Airfield Chi, Valinor Hills, Jezero Crater, Mars (18.44° N, 77.45° E)
data.description: The Wright Brothers moment of another world; completed 72 flights totaling over 128 minutes.
data.discoveries: Aerial scout mapping safe navigation corridors for the Perseverance rover.
data.legacy: Opened the era of planetary aerial flight exploration.

data.name: Phoenix Lander
data.current_location: Green Valley, Vastitas Borealis, Mars (68.2188° N, 234.2508° E)
data.description: First spacecraft to land in the Martian arctic permafrost zone.
data.discoveries: Exposed subsurface white ice trenches that vaporized in sunlight, and identified perchlorate.
data.legacy: Proved the presence of near-surface water ice in the Martian high latitudes.

data.name: InSight Lander
data.description: Stationary geophysical station that listened to the seismic heartbeat of Mars for 4 years.
data.discoveries: Detected magnitude-5 monster marsquakes and measured the size of Mars's molten iron core.
data.legacy: Created humanity's first complete internal geological map of the Red Planet.

data.name: Vikram Lander
data.operational_period: 23 August – 04 September 2023 (1 Lunar Day / 14 Earth Days)
data.current_location: Shiv Shakti Point, between Manzinus C and Simpelius N craters, Moon (69.373° S, 32.319° E)
data.description: Vikram is the ISRO lander that achieved humanity’s first successful soft landing in the lunar south polar region on 23 August 2023. Touchdown occurred at Shiv Shakti Point (69.37° S). Named after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the lander operated for one lunar day, deploying the Pragyan rover and executing a historic hop experiment before entering planned sleep.
data.legacy: Made India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to land near the lunar south pole; proved high-precision autonomous hazard-avoidance landing technology.

data.name: Pragyan Rover
data.current_location: Shiv Shakti Point, high southern latitude, Moon (69.373° S, 32.319° E)
data.description: Pragyan is the 26-kilogram lunar rover that rolled down Vikram’s ramp onto the lunar south polar surface on 23 August 2023. Over the course of 10 Earth days, it traversed 101.4 meters, avoiding craters and conducting the first direct spectroscopy of untouched south polar regolith.
data.legacy: First rover to operate near the lunar south pole; provided unprecedented ground-truth geochemical data validating satellite spectral observations.

data.name: Rosetta Spacecraft
data.current_location: Ma’at region pit walls, small lobe, Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko
data.description: Rosetta was the landmark European Space Agency mission that achieved the first orbit around a comet nucleus. Launched in 2004, it travelled for a decade across 6.4 billion kilometers before rendezvousing with comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko in August 2014. It deployed the Philae lander and studied the comet for two years as it rounded the Sun.
data.legacy: A triumph of European space engineering; completely transformed cometary science and planetary formation models.

data.name: New Horizons Spacecraft
data.current_location: Outer Kuiper Belt (~58 AU / 8.7 billion km from the Sun)
data.description: Flew past Pluto at 49,600 km/h in July 2015, then visited contact binary Arrokoth in 2019.
data.discoveries: Captured the iconic heart-shaped nitrogen glacier (Sputnik Planitia) on Pluto.
data.legacy: Currently exploring the distant outer heliosphere boundary alongside Voyagers.

data.name: Zhurong Rover
data.current_location: Southern Utopia Planitia, Mars (25.10° N, 109.90° E)
data.description: First Chinese Mars rover, drove 1,921 meters across the vast northern lowlands.
data.discoveries: Detected layered subsurface structures indicative of ancient sedimentary floods.
data.legacy: Marks China's arrival as a major rover operator on Mars, resting in Utopia Planitia.

data.name: SLIM Lander
data.current_location: Shioli Crater rim slope, Moon (13.3160° S, 25.2510° E)
data.description: Achieved unprecedented pinpoint landing accuracy, touching down just 55 meters from its target.
data.discoveries: Survived three brutal -130°C lunar nights and transmitted high-res spectroscopy of lunar olivine.
data.legacy: Established Japan as the 5th nation to soft-land on the Moon, resting at Shioli Crater.
